front: Which famous ocean liner sank on April 15, 1912 after hitting an iceberg?
back: RMS Titanic — it sank on its maiden voyage in the North Atlantic, killing over 1,500 people

front: What was the name of the Spanish galleon that sank off Florida in 1622 and was found by Mel Fisher in 1985?
back: Nuestra Señora de Atocha — it carried an estimated $450 million in treasure

front: Which Swedish warship sank in Stockholm harbor on its maiden voyage in 1628?
back: Vasa — it capsized and sank just 1,300 meters into its first journey due to being top-heavy

front: What British luxury liner was torpedoed by a German U-boat in 1915, helping draw the US into WWI?
back: RMS Lusitania — sank off the coast of Ireland, killing 1,198 people

front: Which ship carried treasure from the Spanish Empire and sank near Cartagena, Colombia in 1708?
back: San José — often called the 'Holy Grail of shipwrecks,' its cargo is estimated at billions of dollars

front: What famous pirate ship, captained by Blackbeard, ran aground off North Carolina in 1718?
back: Queen Anne's Revenge — its wreck was discovered in 1996 near Beaufort Inlet

front: Which passenger ferry sank in the Baltic Sea in 1994, killing 852 people?
back: MS Estonia — one of the deadliest maritime disasters in European waters

front: What was the name of the ship that explorer Ernest Shackleton lost in Antarctic ice in 1915?
back: Endurance — it was crushed by pack ice in the Weddell Sea; its wreck was found in 2022

front: Which Japanese battleship, the largest ever built, was sunk by US aircraft in 1945?
back: Yamato — it was sunk during Operation Ten-Go while heading to Okinawa

front: What German battleship was scuttled by its crew in 1919 at Scapa Flow, Scotland?
back: SMS Bayern — part of the mass scuttling of the German High Seas Fleet after WWI

front: Which ship carried the Liberty Bell replica and sank in Lake Michigan in 1860?
back: Lady Elgin — an excursion steamer that collided with a lumber schooner, killing about 300 people

front: What famous ship did explorer Henry Hudson use to search for the Northwest Passage?
back: Discovery — Hudson's crew mutinied in 1611 and set him adrift in Hudson Bay

front: Which ocean liner was deliberately sunk as an artificial reef off the coast of Florida in 2006?
back: USNS General Hoyt S. Vandenberg — now one of the world's largest artificial reefs

front: What WWI hospital ship was torpedoed in the English Channel in 1916?
back: HMHS Britannic — Titanic's sister ship, sank in the Aegean Sea (not English Channel) after hitting a mine in 1916

front: Which Portuguese ship sank in 1606 near Mozambique carrying treasures from India?
back: São João Baptista — one of many Portuguese carracks lost on the Carreira da Índia route

front: What Arctic exploration ship was trapped in ice and abandoned in 1845?
back: HMS Erebus — part of Franklin's lost expedition; its wreck was found in 2014 in the Canadian Arctic

front: Which cruise ship capsized off the Italian island of Giglio in 2012?
back: Costa Concordia — Captain Francesco Schettino was convicted of manslaughter for 32 deaths

front: What ancient Greek merchant ship, dating to 300 BC, was found off the coast of Cyprus?
back: Kyrenia ship — one of the best-preserved ancient shipwrecks, now displayed in a museum in Cyprus

front: Which ironclad warship was the first to sink another ship using a torpedo in combat, in 1878?
back: HMS Shah did not sink its target; the first torpedo sinking was by a Russian torpedo boat against the Ottoman ship Intibah in 1878

front: What famous Dutch East India Company ship sank off Western Australia in 1629?
back: Batavia — after the wreck, a mutiny and massacre occurred among the survivors

front: Which ship was the subject of the 'most famous maritime mystery' when it was found abandoned in 1872?
back: Mary Celeste — found drifting in the Atlantic with no crew aboard, their fate remains unknown

front: What British warship exploded and sank during the Battle of Jutland in 1916?
back: HMS Queen Mary — it broke apart after its magazines detonated, killing 1,266 crew

front: Which oil tanker ran aground in Alaska in 1989, causing one of the worst oil spills in US history?
back: Exxon Valdez — spilled 11 million gallons of crude oil into Prince William Sound

front: What Confederate submarine was the first to sink an enemy warship in combat?
back: H.L. Hunley — it sank the USS Housatonic in 1864 but was also lost with all hands

front: Which treasure ship sank in a hurricane off Florida in 1715 as part of a Spanish fleet?
back: The 1715 Treasure Fleet — eleven ships were lost, scattering gold and silver along Florida's coast

front: What famous ship was part of Columbus's fleet and ran aground off Haiti in 1492?
back: Santa María — Columbus used its timber to build La Navidad, the first European settlement in the Americas

front: Which luxury liner was sunk by the Italian navy in WWII while being used as a troop transport?
back: SS Rex — the Italian-built Blue Riband holder was sunk by RAF rockets in 1944 in Trieste harbor

front: What ship carrying convicts sank off the coast of Tasmania in 1835?
back: George III — one of Australia's worst convict ship disasters, killing 134 people

front: Which famous warship was Admiral Nelson's flagship and survived the Battle of Trafalgar in 1805?
back: HMS Victory — trick question! Victory survived and is preserved in Portsmouth. Nelson died aboard it.

front: What 17th-century ship was found nearly intact in the Black Sea in 2018, dating to 400 BC?
back: A Greek trading vessel — the oldest intact shipwreck ever discovered, found at 2 km depth where lack of oxygen preserved it
